newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to raise September coffee margin May 20.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to raise September coffee margin May 20.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said on Thursday it will raise the margin on September 1997 coffee contract to $6,000, including a $1,000 spot charge, effective May 20.
The margin required for September 1997 until May 20, is $5,000, the exchange said in a statement.

Effective May 16, CSCE increased the margin required July 1997 coffee "C" contracts to $8,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, while the margins required on all other coffee contracts also increased, rising by $1,000 to $5,000.

In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions require a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are CSCE members or members of the trade. However, the $3,000 spot charge for July 1997 and the $1,000 spot charge for September 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these months, the excahnge said.
For customers who are not exchange members or members of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, the CSCE said.
